# Document Preparation Clause

Prepares a required child document. With `parameters.obtain: create`, beginning preparation asks the system to create a new child that meets the prepared requirements. Supplying an existing child through `provide` is rejected in this mode. With `parameters.obtain: provide` (the default), the designated supplier must provide a matching child that is already initialized and active, for the active request. The plan rejects other values.

`bindings.begin` identifies the connection that starts preparation, and `bindings.resume` identifies the connection that can resume after a dependency is ready. Each can name its own workflow party or be triggered by an event. A workflow connection without an explicit party uses the supplier. `parameters.suppliedBy` is the supplier and must be the party invoking the `bindings.provide` workflow. `parameters.authority` must name the `provider` role, which is separate from the initiation, supply and resume connections.

Provision requires the current request ID, its prepared requirement reference and a child whose source, terms, configuration and participant roster match. A later publication of the same child origin can be supplied, but a different origin cannot replace it. An identical begin request is a duplicate; a different request or changed intent is rejected once preparation exists.

Beginning or supplying a child does not establish readiness. Preparation can resume through a configured connection and rechecks automatically when parent activation or the instruction changes, or when an Amendment Applied event is observed. The normal flow records readiness once the parent is active and the child is initialized and active. The child's own work and any approval it requires are separate from preparation.

The optional inherited `createOn` can also trigger automatic creation on clause initialization or a matching parent state change. If configured, `attachWhen` requires a matching parent state before attachment or creation. Request and instruction paths default to `/attachmentRequest_<key>` and `/instruction_<key>` and must be distinct. The clause permits one-way preparation and declares no child request actions.
